answer: A sequential proof-of-work protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring each network vertex to maintain an unbroken execution thread. Enforcing non-parallelizable hash chains prevents adversaries from running hollow agent swarms on shared hardware. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicating scarce, physical CPU cores per active identity. However, adversaries using specialized high-frequency ASICs gain an unfair computational advantage over commodity systems.
